methodology_notes:
Item 1: every output using the label NOT VERIFIED was credited, even though none displays the full three-way scale. Only V, with 'FAILS the contract', was marked absent for reading as pass/fail. A stricter judge could deny all six.

Item 4: U was credited on thin evidence, the ordered list plus the single 'Minor' tag. V has no severity labels at all, only a 'lower confidence' tag. That split is borderline.

Item 5: X and Z include short regex or fix pointers. I treated them as guidance and not as a corrected implementation, while U and V gave full replacement code. This is the item most open to a different call.

Item 6: U's inline 'gets right' bullets carry some reasoning but include bare assertions. I called it absent because of those bare items. Y's list is similar in depth but cites specifics for each axis, so it was credited. This one could reasonably go the other way.
